Stocks slide as chipmakers drag Wall Street lower

By Jane Rivera

October 13, 2026
Share on X

The S&P 500 fell for a third straight session on Tuesday as a selloff in semiconductor shares outweighed a strong start to the bank earnings season, leaving the index 0.9% below its record close.

Nvidia dropped 3.4% and Broadcom lost 4.1% after its chief executive likened investment in artificial intelligence to a casino, comments that rattled a sector that has carried the market for most of the year.

Banks were a bright spot. JPMorgan Chase rose 1.2% after reporting a jump in trading revenue, while Citigroup gained 0.8% even as it warned that higher interest rates could weigh on lending later in the year.

Bond yields in focus

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note slipped to 5.21% from 5.29% a day earlier, easing some of the pressure on growth stocks, though analysts said inflation data due on Thursday remains the next big test for markets.

  • The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4% to 51,102.
  • The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.3%, its worst day in a month.
